text:
maria: quick sketch: crash-safe prefetched-prefix handoff protocol. wanted to sanity-check before RFC.

kai: short version?

maria: old owner should enter a soft-drain state, attach a tiny "marker" to the prefix (owner id + epoch + drain flag). new owner does guarded dual-reads until marker clears. separate async reconciler fixes any missed writes.

alex: how do we keep steady-state perf low? sounds like an extra read hop.

maria: runtime consults marker only on misses or lease-change—normal cache hits are unaffected. marker encoding is compact. dual-read happens only for misses during/just-after handoff.

kai: leader crash mid-handoff?
maria: lease tokens in metastore with CAS. marker includes epoch so any mismatch is detectable; new leader either extends or aborts based on CAS outcome.

alex: hot-flipping prefixes could cause churn. mitigation?
maria: TTL for markers, probabilistic reconciler backoff, and per-tenant caps. also emit metrics to detect pathological flip rates.

ops-bot: deploy-bot recommends metrics: ["prefix_handoff_start","prefix_handoff_fail","marker_set","marker_clear","dual_read_count","handoff_ms","hotflip_rate"]. alert on handoff_fail spike or hotflip_rate > threshold. :bell:

maria: next actions: i'll write RFC + failure modes; kai will prototype marker header and tests; alex will perf the dual-read path; ops to draft reconciler playbook.

kai: ensure we preserve client-visible semantics (no lost writes).

maria: yep, RFC will include litmus tests and a staged rollout plan.

alex: ack. schedule design review when draft is ready.
